memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"So Moses told this to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites"
- Lev 21:24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A simple closing line, easy to skim past. But look at who heard it.
Moses did not deliver these priestly regulations privately to Aaron
and his sons. He told all the Israelites.

Why would ordinary farmers and mothers and children need to know the
rules for priests? Because God's people were meant to understand the
holiness of the God they worshipped. The whole nation needed to grasp
why the priest lived as he did, and what it said about the One he
served.

There is a principle here about God's Word. It is not meant to be
locked away with a few experts. God gives His revelation to His whole
people. Luke praised the Bereans for examining the Scriptures
themselves (Acts 17:11). Paul told Timothy that all Scripture is
God-breathed and useful (2 Tim 3:16) - including chapters like this one.

Dear reader, do not skip the hard parts of your Bible. Chapters like
Leviticus 21 are difficult, but they show us a God of overwhelming
holiness, and they make the cross shine all the brighter.

Read it all. It was given to you too.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are there parts of Scripture I avoid because they are difficult?
2. What has this chapter taught me about God's holiness?
3. How can I make regular Bible reading a settled habit?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You for giving Your whole Word to Your whole people.
Give me hunger for it, even the hard parts, and let it lead me to
Christ. Amen.
